extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners; KIPO patent office staff; patent attorneys and applicants interacting with KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Official Korean Intellectual Property Office examination procedure and guidelines describing how patent applications are to be searched, examined, notified, amended, reexamined, and handled by examiners. Covers examiner qualifications, IPC assignment, search procedures, notices of rejection, amendments (including ex officio), reexamination, interviews and document delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of Formal Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination of formal requirements is a process to check as to whether an application meets the formal requirements. The followings relates to the requirements: capacity, representation, physical requirements of the application, filing and fees, matters according to each subparagraph of the Article 11 (1) of the Enforcement Rules of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary check is in principle carried out in the name of the Commissioner of KIPO by the receiving office where application documents are initially filed. When the receiving office fails to conduct the examination of formal requirements, an examiner can carry out further checks in the name of the Commissioner of KIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of International Patent Classification (IPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification of a patent application is performed with taking into consideration the invention as claimed. It is necessary as an effective search tool for the retrieval of patent documents by intellectual property offices and other users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO adopts the IPC, a hierarchical patent classification under WIPO control. Classification decisions should reflect the scope of the claimed invention and may use detailed description if scope unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laying-open of Application (Publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be laid open in the Patent Gazette as soon as after the expiry of a period of eighteen months from the date of filing, where priority if claimed, from the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application may be published earlier if requested by the applicant. Some applications treated 'confidential' may be excluded from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Examination — Timing and Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is examined only when a request for examination is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person can request examination within 5 years for a patent application (or 3 years for a registered utility model application filed after 10.01,2006) from the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of Examination — Purpose and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of examination is to ensure that the application and the invention to which it relates meet the requirements set out in the relevant Articles of the Patent Act (Article 46 or 62).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prime task of the examiner is to deal with the substantive requirement; if formalities are incorrect or incomplete, the examiner may invite an applicant to correct such formal deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Grounds for Rejection — Duty to Explain and Invite Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner shall write to the applicant giving reasons for any objections he raises under any subparagraphs of the Article 62, and invite the applicant within a specified period to submit arguments before final decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices include types (Non-final Notice of Grounds for Rejection, Final Notice of Grounds for Rejection), selection rules, instructions for written notice and preparation of written decision of rejection, and claim-by-claim examination guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments/Arguments by Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit arguments in response to an examiner's notice of grounds for rejection and may file amendments to the specification (including detailed description and claims) or drawing(s) within the period designated in Article 47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are considered by examiner in subsequent examination; scope and timing of amendments are governed by statutory limits (Article 47) and further described in Parts dealing with amendment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination after Amendments/Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking account of any amendments proposed, or arguments made, by the applicant in reply to the notice of grounds for rejection, the examiner should examine the application again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may discover new grounds and must notify newly found grounds for rejection if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to Grant a Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner finds no grounds to reject a patent application, he decides that a Korean patent be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding to grant, examiner may also amend clearly erroneous matters ex officio (see Amendment Ex Officio) and must notify applicant of such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to Refuse (Reject) an Application
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner examines the application again with taking account of any amendments or arguments in reply to the notice of grounds for rejection and considers that the applicant has not overcome his objections, the examiner may decide to refuse the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedures for delivering decisions and further appeal or reexamination rights for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and Request for Reexamination — Timing and Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend a specification or drawing(s) to request for reexamination within 30 days from the receipt of a certified copy of the decision to reject a patent (or the extension period if the statutory period is extended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination request cancels the previous decision of rejection; reexamination is not allowed where there is a prior decision of rejection after reexamination or where there is a request for a trial against the decision for rejection. Where both amendment and trial request submitted same day, examiner treats amendment timing specially and may return amendment if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case where a request for reexamination is made, the examiner shall take into consideration any amendment provided by the applicant and re-examine the application according to the general examination procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination cancels previous rejection but prior procedural acts remain valid; scope of amendments upon reexamination is same as amendment according to final notification; examiner must review amendment appropriateness and may dismiss inappropriate amendments under statutory criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment Ex Officio — Authority and Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a decision to grant a patent, an examiner may amend ex officio the matters in the specification, drawing(s), or abstract attached to a patent application notice that is clearly erroneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment ex officio limited to self-evident errors (misspells, omissions, inconsistent reference signs) that do not influence substantive scope of rights and have no possibility of alternative interpretation. Examiner shall notify applicant of matters to be amended ex officio along with certified copy of decision to grant; applicant may accept or oppose before payment of patent fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters to be Amended Ex Officio — Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters that are 'clearly erroneous' in the description, drawing(s), or abstract refer to matters that do not fall under the grounds for rejection and do not influence the substantive scope of right in the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include misspelling or missing words according to standard Korean, inconsistent use of reference signs in drawings, redundant writing, errors in drawing explanations (misstated drawing numbers), misspelling in summary tables, and inconsistency in title between description and application. Examiner must ensure no possibility of different interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions of Amendment Ex Officio — Prohibitions and Cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: The matters to be amended ex officio are limited to self-evident error. When an examiner amends ex officio, he/she should not alter the scope of the claim, and the amendment ex officio shall not be allowed if there arises any possibility of different interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If misstatement is a ground for rejection, no ex officio amendment allowed; when both ex officio matters and grounds for rejection exist, notify grounds for rejection and reference ex officio matters; examiner shall not add new matters; cannot amend errors referring to deleted claims; be careful with uses like 'the said' without clear specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure of Amendment Ex Officio — Notice and Applicant's Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner intending to amend ex officio shall notify the matters to be amended to the applicant with a certified copy of the decision to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must describe specifically where and why to amend (use ID numbers or page/line references). If applicant opposes ex officio amendment in whole or part, they may submit written argument before payment of patent fee; opposed matters deemed never to have existed and published description will reflect applicant's choice. Illegitimate ex officio amendment published is deemed never to have existed unless later recognized as legitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: A person eligible to become a patent examiner shall be the following public officials in KIPO or its affiliated agencies who have completed the prescribed education and training course for a trial examiner conducted by International Intellectual Property Training Institute (IIPTI); A public official of Grade V or higher in general service, a public official in general service who belongs to the Senior Civil Service, or a specialized contract-based public official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grade of examiner is decided by experience, assessment, and training; chief examiner requires more than 10 years, senior more than 7 years, junior more than 4 years, together with completion of required training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall proceed the examination with speed and accuracy in accordance with the Patent Act and its related provisions, and examine independently based on legal and technical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New examiners serve as assistant examiners for up to 6 months then joint examination for another 6 months; primary examiner may consult other examiners for convergence technologies or foreign language expertise; director general may convene joint conferences for difficult unified rule application; confidentiality duties per State Public Officials Act apply; documents not to be disclosed except for specified purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and Change of Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more examiner shall be designated for each IPC and be in charge of the designated examination; one among them shall be designated as a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner designation by Patent Examination Support Division; if examiner transfers post-first-notification, they continue examination; reexamination or returned applications should be examined by same examiner unless justifiable reason; generally an examiner should not be in charge of same IPC for 5 consecutive years; conflicts of interest rules exclude certain examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Reporting Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall report to appropriate superiors when issuing certain actions (notification of grounds for rejection, decision to grant, revocation, rulings, invalidation measures, accelerated examination rulings, requests for correction regarding serious deficiencies, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting chain varies by grade; specific cases where reporting can be exempted are listed for junior, senior, and chief examiners. Report to general director of examination bureau or head of unit as per the action and grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Name of Authority for Examination-related Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If KIPO determines a due form for certain documents to be submitted, it is principle to use the due form; if none designated, use a general document form in accordance with Instruction on Office Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is attached document, list attachments at end of document body. Patent examination shall be conducted in the name of the examiner in charge except for specified exceptions; joint examinations carry joint names of examiners concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC Assignment — General Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical subject-matter stated in the claimed invention of an application are classified into IPC symbols comprised of section, class, subclass, main group and sub-group. The classification shall be made on the basis of the scope of the claimed invention; when scope unclear, base on detailed description; some subject-matter not in claims but in description can form basis for classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple technical subject-matters exist, core subject-matter becomes 'main classification' and others 'sub-classification'; if unity lacking, claim 1 can be basis; indexing code and additional information rules; divisional/converted application classification should generally follow earlier application unless obviously different.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC Assignment by Technical Subject (Apparatus/Method/Product/Multistage)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, classification place for either an apparatus or a method shall be used if pertinent; if no place for apparatus, use method; if neither, use product or function-oriented place; multistage processes or plants classified with place pertinent to composition or output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composition constituents have individual characteristics, each constituent may be classified; where composition has no intrinsic characteristics but its constituent has, the constituent classification applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for Prior Art — Scope and Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Search procedure includes defining search scope, conditions under which search is not required or limited, time coverage of search, suspension, general principle of search, citation of prior art documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search scope should be determined in light of claimed invention and IPC assignments; special provisions for when search may be limited or suspended; guidelines for citing prior art include patent, non-patent, and electronic documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures after Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions required after conducting prior art searches, including how to handle identified documents and integrate search results into examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes possible additional search requests, delivery and review of search outcomes, and decision-making based on search results (e.g., forming grounds for rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for Prior Art by Specialized Search Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for requesting prior art search by specialized search organizations and handling their outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains instructions on search requests and delivery/review of search outcome by examiner and possible uses of such specialized searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must understand the invention as claimed and as described to conduct substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding guides IPC assignment, search strategy, claim interpretation and determination of prior art relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Prior Art Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must review cited prior art documents in relation to the claimed invention to determine novelty, inventive step, and other statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for disclosure of information on prior art documents (citation of patent/non-patent/electronic documents) and how to reflect such citations in notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Application Handling (Priority, Non-prejudicial Disclosures, Divisional, Entitled Persons, International)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules apply for priority claims under treaty, domestic priority claims, non-prejudicial disclosures, divisional or converted applications, application by entitled person, and international patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each special application type has procedural and evidentiary requirements described (e.g., dates, documents, effects on examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on a Claim-by-claim Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination may be carried out on a claim-by-claim basis with specific purpose and instructions for written notice of grounds for rejection and preparation of written decision of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how to prepare notices per claim, when to select claim-by-claim examination and instructions for documenting the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Prior Art Documents — Patent, Non-patent and Electronic
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to cite prior art: patent documents, non-patent literature, and electronic documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies citation formats, disclosure obligations, and how to handle electronic source identification and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for Written Argument and Treatment of Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes extension or reduction of designated period, instructions for written argument submission, treatment of amendments, and method to confirm amendment of description, claims and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers extension/approval rules for substantive and formality examination periods, when to allow reductions, and how to process and confirm content of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance when an additional search is necessary during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When initial search does not suffice to resolve patentability issues, examiner may order additional search and proceed according to search outcome procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Deferral or Extension of Processing Period
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules allowing examination deferral or extension of processing period under defined conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how to grant deferrals or extensions and the effects on other proceedings and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Delivery — General Principles and Public Notification
rubrics_metrics.description: General principles governing delivery of documents and procedures for delivery by public notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains acceptable methods of delivery, when public notification may be used, and legal effects of such deliveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Interview Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for request and grant of personal interviews, procedures of personal interview, instructions for personal interview and interviews on visit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how applicants request interviews, when interviews are granted, how to conduct them, and how record and follow-up are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Amendment (General and Reexamination Context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope and admissibility of amendments are governed by statutory limits (Article 47 etc.) and examined for appropriateness both in ordinary examination and reexamination contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing amendment appropriateness, compare additions to original specification/drawings; in reexamination consider previously dismissed amendments differently; an examiner shall not dismiss an amendment retroactively if previously accepted for reexamination protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Amendment Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: In reexamination or amendment submissions, the examiner shall judge whether an amendment is appropriate by comparing added matter to the original application and to any intermediate amended specification as required by Article 47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different scenarios (amendment before/after dismissal, sequences of amendments) specify which documents form the basis for comparison; protects applicant confidence by limiting retroactive dismissal in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination after Admission or Dismissal of Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is admitted, examiner shall reflect the amendment and decide whether grounds for rejection remain; where dismissed, examiner proceeds with pre-amendment specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If admitted amendment still leaves objections, examiner may reject; if admission reveals other un-notified grounds, examiner must notify new grounds; dismissal leads to immediate resumption with original specification and potential rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for Reexamination (procedural protections and effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the request for reexamination is filed, the decision to reject a patent application is regarded as cancelled; applicants may not withdraw reexamination requests and there are procedural limits on other filings during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant cannot both pursue trial and reexamination simultaneously; withdrawal of reexamination is treated as uncertain document and returned after opportunity to explain; reexamination request prevents filing of certain documents within statutory periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment Ex Officio — Specific Limitations and Examples of Prohibited Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment ex officio is intended for obvious errors only and is subject to strict limits so it does not change claim scope or create new technical matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited: ex officio amendment if matter is ground for rejection; adding new matter in description or drawings; altering scope of claims; amending references to deleted claims; any amendment that could lead to different interpretations. Examiner should notify reasons and locations precisely; applicant's opposition means amended matters are treated as never having existed in published description.
